argument: When treatment allocation, model choice, or stopping depends on accumulating data, ordinary fixed-design estimators and p-values can become biased or miscalibrated. Valid inference must condition on, model, or explicitly protect against the adaptive policy using randomization, martingales, confidence sequences, or selective-inference corrections.
boundary: Different adaptive mechanisms require different corrections.
Validity can be conservative when adaptation is weak.
Inference after opaque automated policies may be difficult without complete logs.
claim: When treatment allocation, model choice, or stopping depends on accumulating data, ordinary fixed-design estimators and p-values can become biased or miscalibrated. Valid inference must condition on, model, or explicitly protect against the adaptive policy using randomization, martingales, confidence sequences, or selective-inference corrections.
interpretation: Principia should retain the complete adaptive policy and stopping trace. A final dataset alone may be insufficient to reconstruct valid inference.
